SparkSustain Manual

The Spark canvases near your desk follow your MacBook — on when you're working at the office, dark when you're not.

How it decides

SparkSustain applies one simple rule, re-checked every time your Mac wakes, sleeps, or changes network:

Your MacBookAt the office?Your Sparks
Awake, screens onYesOn, at your wake brightness
Awake, screens onNo — awayOff (dark)
Asleep / lid closedAnywhereOff (dark)

"At the office" means your Mac's network matches the one you captured with Set Current Network as Office. Commands go through Videri's cloud APIs using your own developer API key — nothing is installed on the Sparks.

Optionally, you can make being at your desk part of the rule: Require Current Power Source (Desk) captures the power adapter your Mac is plugged into (say, your USB-C monitor or dock). From then on the Sparks only come up when the Mac is drawing power from that exact source — on MagSafe, battery, or any other charger they stay dark, even on the office network.

The menu bar icon shows the current state: ☀️ awake at the office · 🚫 awake but away · 🌙 asleep.

The menu, item by item

Status lines (top)
The first line reports the last action taken and why; the second shows the office network and whether you're on it.
Automation Enabled
Uncheck to pause all automatic changes — handy when someone is presenting on your Sparks. Re-checking immediately re-syncs.
Set Current Network as Office
Records the network you're on right now as "the office." Re-run it any time you move desks or the office network changes.
Require Current Power Source (Desk)
Optional: captures the adapter currently powering your Mac as a wake requirement — unplugged, on battery, or on a different charger, the Sparks stay dark. Click again ("Stop Requiring Desk Power") to remove the requirement.
Hold Wake Brightness / Hold Screens Off
Pin a state for a chosen time — 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, until end of day, or until you resume automation. The hold beats all automation rules until it expires; the menu shows the active hold and a Resume Automation Now item ends it early. The keyboard toggle holds for 60 minutes by default.
Wake Brightness ▸
Choose the brightness (10–100%) your Sparks run at while you're working. Applies immediately if you're in the wake state.
Run Setup Assistant…
Re-runs the guided setup: credentials, Spark selection, office network. Safe to run any time — your existing choices are pre-filled.
Discover Canvases…
Fetches every canvas your account can see into a reference file and opens it.
Help
Opens this manual.
View Log
Opens the activity log — one line per event and per-Spark command result.
Start at Login
Keeps SparkSustain running automatically. Recommended: automation only works while the app is running.

Keyboard shortcut

Press ⌃⌥S (Control + Option + S) from any app to toggle all your Sparks between on and off. Works even when the menu is closed.

First-time setup

  1. Create an API key at developer.videri.com/dashboard (log in → API Keys tab → create → copy it immediately, it's shown once). No developer account? Ask the platform team.
  2. Launch SparkSustain — the Setup Assistant opens on first run and walks you through: pasting your credentials (verified live, so typos are caught), choosing your workspaces from a tree (including nested sub-workspaces) that scopes what SparkSustain may see and control, checking off your Sparks from a searchable list, capturing the office network, optionally requiring your desk power source — with a quick unplug/reconnect verification so SparkSustain proves it can tell when you leave — and the first sync.
Your username, password, and API key are stored only on your Mac, in a file readable only by your account. They are sent solely to Videri's own API.
Brightness schedule takeover: when you confirm your Spark selection, SparkSustain warns you and then permanently deletes any existing brightness schedules on those specific displays from the Videri platform, so they can't fight its on/off control. The managed displays are then set to their new default state: 0% brightness / display off — they only light up while your Mac meets the wake conditions. Other displays are untouched. SparkSustain then enforces its own state perpetually — re-asserting it every 10 minutes — so a Spark that reboots, misses a command, or gets adjusted elsewhere is pulled back within minutes.

What's new in 1.2

  • Brightness schedule takeover — with warning, platform schedules on managed displays are deleted and the displays default to 0% / off.
  • Perpetual enforcement — the decided state is re-asserted every 10 minutes; displays stay in their state until the Mac meets the wake conditions.
  • Desk power requirement — optional wake condition tied to your desk charger/dock; disconnecting it darkens the Sparks within ~3 seconds. Now part of the Setup Assistant, with detect-now or decide-later.

Troubleshooting

"Couldn't sign in" during setup

Re-check username, password, and API key. Keys created with an expiry date stop working when it passes — create a fresh key.

Sparks don't react

Open View Log: every command logs a named OK/FAILED line per Spark. DEVICE_OFFLINE means that Spark has no network — check its connection. Re-run Run Setup Assistant… to confirm the right Sparks are selected.

Sparks came on while I was away

Check the office network line in the menu — if it says "not set (automating everywhere)", capture your office network with Set Current Network as Office.

macOS blocks the app at install

Right-click the installer → Open → Open (needed once for downloaded files), or System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.

Files SparkSustain uses

  • ~/Library/Application Support/SparkSustain/config.json — settings and credentials (private to your account)
  • ~/Library/Application Support/SparkSustain/canvases.json — the canvas list from Discover Canvases
  • ~/Library/Logs/SparkSustain.log — the activity log

Uninstalling

  1. Menu bar icon → uncheck Start at Login, then Quit SparkSustain.
  2. Delete ~/Applications/SparkSustain.app.
  3. Optionally delete the folder ~/Library/Application Support/SparkSustain (this removes your stored credentials).
